summary: Facebook Live test passed, backend only. (1) Real Facebook stream over rtmps via the local TLS relay (SECS=45): start 200, platforms ['facebook'], live=True on all 3 polls, no ffmpeg errors in the log, stop OK. The history entry was logged and the destinations were cleared. (2) Invalid key 'FB-invalid-123' with rtmps://live-api-s.facebook.com:443/rtmp via the PUBLIC URL: 422 application/json after 3.1s with the friendly detail ('The platform refused the stream. Check that your stream key is correct...'). Status live=False with last_error set. No relay listeners leaked. History unchanged (same latest id, count 18 -> 18). (3) YouTube + Facebook together for 30s: start 200, platforms ['youtube','facebook'], live=True on all 3 polls, stop OK, keys cleared. No leftover tee ffmpeg or 127.0.0.1 listeners. (4) pytest /app/backend/tests: 24/24 passed. (5) Extra check, valid YouTube key + invalid Facebook key: start returns 200 and status reports live with platforms ['youtube','facebook'], though ffmpeg dropped the Facebook output ('continuing with 1/2 slaves'). See the minor issues.

minor.issue: Partial failure is silent with multiple destinations. tee uses onfail=ignore, so with one bad key (FB-invalid-123) and one good key (YouTube) the start returns 200 and status says live with platforms ['youtube','facebook'], while the Facebook output has already failed ('Slave muxer #1 failed ... continuing with 1/2 slaves'). The user believes they are live on Facebook when they are not.

The 'log' field returns raw ffmpeg stderr, which contains the full relay URL including the stream key (e.g. rtmp://127.0.0.1:34183/rtmp/<KEY>). It leaks the key to the frontend/UI and is not user-friendly. Mask keys or don't expose raw log lines.

action_items: Optional: detect per-output failure. Parse 'Slave ... failed' lines from the tee log and expose a per-platform state (e.g. failed_platforms / platforms reduced to the working ones), or return a 422/warning if any output fails in the 3s start window.
Optional: mask stream keys in status.log, or drop raw ffmpeg lines from the API response.
critical_code_review_comments: streamer.status reports 'platforms' from configuration, not from the actual live outputs. Combined with onfail=ignore this hides partial failures.
relay.handle swallows upstream connect/TLS errors without logging, so Facebook TLS/DNS problems are invisible in backend logs.
Carried over: friendly_error's broad 'Connection' match; history capped at 20 (to_list(20)); stream key visible in ffmpeg argv (ps).
